name: Dark Traits
subtitle: Dark Triad
instructions: Rate each statement from 1 (Not at all like me) to 5 (Very much like me), based on how you genuinely think and behave. There are no good or bad answers here.

questions.text: There are things about yourself, your plans, your opinions of certain people, that you wantedly keep to yourself even around people you're close to.
When you want something from someone, you know or think you know how to approach the request in a way that makes it easier for them to say yes.
Before doing something important, you think of whose support you would want behind you first.
When someone does something that genuinely bothers you, you often find it more useful to stay pleasant with them for now.
You have a fairly reliable memory for the moments when people have shown you who they really are, and you keep that in mind.
When someone does something wrong by you, you rarely feel the need to respond immediately. You trust the timing to work itself out.
Even with people you're quite open with, there are areas of your thinking that you don't let them into.
When you're deciding how to act in a situation, how it affects you tends to be a fairly central part of the calculation.
Over time, you've noticed that most people follow fairly predictable patterns, and you find that awareness useful.
In most situations you're part of, people tend to look to you when something needs to be figured out or decided.
Being the person that a room is focused on isn't something that particularly appeals to you.
When you're not around, you sometimes have a sense that the dynamic in a group shifts in some way.
People in your life have pointed out that there's something distinct about the way you carry yourself or how you come across.
You find yourself naturally drawn to spending time around people who are accomplished or well-regarded in what they do.
When someone praises your work directly, you tend to feel a little uncomfortable rather than straightforwardly pleased.
More than once, someone has drawn a comparison between you and a well-known or particularly capable person.
If you're honest, you think of yourself as fairly ordinary and not particularly different from most people around you.
When you feel that your effort or contribution isn't being acknowledged as it deserves, it genuinely bothers you.
When someone in a position of authority has treated you unfairly, you've felt a clear pull toward wanting to set things straight.
Before making a significant move, you tend to think carefully about the risks and what you might lose.
When you feel wronged, you tend to think that a clear and relatively quick response is better than a slow, drawn-out one.
People who know you well have described you as someone who doesn't always stick to the expected way of doing things.
You tend to say what you think fairly directly, without always softening it for the other person.
People who have pushed against you have generally found it wasn't particularly worth their while.
Your history with rules and authority has been fairly unremarkable, with no real incidents to speak of.
When there is clear mutual interest, physical closeness with someone you've only just met isn't something that would make you particularly uncomfortable.
When you need something badly enough, you're capable of saying what's needed to move things forward, even if it's not the whole picture.
